subject: PYTHON_MINIMIZATION_BASELINE zero_targets.VECTOR: migration path for shared_layer/local/vector_store.py (535 LOC, sole file in the VECTOR bucket)
invariant: main-system/config/python-minimization-baseline.json zero_targets.VECTOR = 1 file / 535 LOC; test_zero_targets_only_shrink enforces tighten-only. Codex B4/B131: production VECTOR responsibility belongs to the Rust engine (vectord). Implementation-side cannot delete the governed degraded path unilaterally: the degraded-mode cache contract (canonical:false, reconciliation_required:true, pending-mutation replay) is authority-shaped behavior requiring governor adjudication.

target_file.storage: PostgreSQL schema gptbridge_rag via pg_adapter (3 tables: collection_meta, collection_point, collection_state)
public_surface: ensure_collection(vector_size) — declares dimension; mismatch raises RAG_VECTOR_DIMENSION_MISMATCH
reconcile_dimension(vector_size, index_version) — explicit cache rebuild, epoch++ (never implicit)
replace_document(document_id, points, module_id) — delete+insert; f64-LE BLOB vectors; text points embedded via blake2b 3-gram hashing (_token_vector, dim 256)
query(vector, limit, module_ids) — module-scoped SQL candidate ceiling + cosine scoring (native_kernel .pyd optional accel)
status() — dict {available, engine:'local-vector-degraded-cache', canonical:False, reconciliation_required:True, points, epoch, index_version, ...}

consumers: main-system/src-core/core_system/rag/degraded_backend.py — DegradedRagBackend (wraps pipeline; calls vector_store.delete_resource — see latent_defect)
architectural_constraint: Degraded mode exists when canonical vectord/PostgreSQL RAG is unavailable. LocalVectorStore persists into PostgreSQL (schema gptbridge_rag), so the degraded path already requires PG. Hosting the degraded cache inside vectord is NOT viable (vectord is the very thing that may be down); vectord-rs file persistence (persist_snapshot/load_snapshot in main.rs/store.rs) only covers vectord's own derived index.

latent_defect.defect: degraded delete_resource is entirely non-functional: (a) line 117 calls self.pipeline.repository.delete_resource(request.resource_id) — LocalRagRepository has NO delete method at all (only existing_document/document_source/replace_document/keyword_search/status), so the call raises AttributeError; (b) line 118 calls self.pipeline.vector_store.delete_resource(...) — LocalVectorStore has only delete(document_id). The first AttributeError is swallowed by the surrounding try/except and returns success=False, so EVERY degraded delete silently fails: document rows, chunk rows, index-state rows and cached vectors of deleted documents all linger (stale-hit surface in a non-canonical store).
latent_defect.implication: the degraded store pair has never actually deleted anything in production — both the vector layer and the repository lack working delete; this is additional evidence the degraded path should be redesigned (lexical repository + a real delete_document), not preserved as-is
latent_defect.loc_equilibrium_note: all nine zero_target buckets sit exactly at baseline (ratchet is strict-greater-than); any fix that adds Python LOC outside allowed zones must be offset by equal-or-greater deletion in the same change — the retire-vector-layer option provides -535 LOC of headroom, comfortably covering the ~15 LOC needed for LocalRagRepository.delete_document + the consumer migrations

options.action: Retire the degraded vector cache entirely: degraded retrieval falls back to bounded lexical search over LocalRagRepository.keyword_search (already exists, already PG-backed, already holds the degraded documents with reassembled content). Add LocalRagRepository.delete_document (~15 LOC: DELETE on the 3 tables) so degraded delete actually works; rewrite DegradedRagBackend.delete_resource onto it; point pipeline_degraded.query at keyword_search. Remove vector_store.py (-535 LOC, VECTOR bucket -> 0 files / 0 LOC). Pending-mutation ledger semantics unchanged; reconciliation replays canonically on recovery as today. Net bucket delta: ~-520 LOC across VECTOR(-535)/RAG(+15).
options.behavior_delta: degraded query results become lexical-ranked instead of embedding-similarity-ranked; stale-vector-cache failure mode eliminated
options.requires: governor adjudication that degraded-mode similarity ranking is non-essential (cache was non-authoritative by contract)

options.action: Implement the degraded vector store natively (C ABI or vectord-side embedded store) with the same ensure/replace/query/delete/status surface and PG or file persistence; Python LocalVectorStore deleted after parity evidence lands.
options.requires: new native artifact + parity suite; heavier; only justified if governor rules similarity ranking IS required in degraded mode

options.action: Reclassify the file out of VECTOR into an allowed zone, or accept it as permanent governed Python (contradicts B4/B131 direction; ratchet stays at 535)

rationale: The store is explicitly non-canonical ('must not be treated as cross-module semantic authority'), every mutation is already replayed through pending_rag_mutation on recovery, the deleted-resource path is already silently broken (latent_defect), and lexical retrieval over LocalRagRepository preserves bounded degraded-mode functionality with zero similarity-ranking authority. It is the only option that both zeroes the VECTOR bucket and removes a failure mode rather than relocating it.
requested_governor_actions: adjudicate whether degraded-mode embedding-similarity retrieval is required (drives retire-vector-layer vs native-degraded-store)
if retire-vector-layer: authorize removal of vector_store.py + the delete_resource call-site fix and the consumer migrations (pipeline_degraded lexical query, local-model RAG fallback)
record adjudication so python-minimization baseline zero_targets.VECTOR can be tightened to 0/0
